The papers do not state why they use carbonate electrolytes with their sodium metal. However, they do mention that carbonate electrolytes are not suitable for sodium metal due to the instability of the organic solid-electrolyte interface (SEI) formed. 

In the first paper, it is mentioned that sodium metal is less stable with carbonate electrolytes than lithium metal, due to the organic SEI formed. 

In the second paper, it is mentioned that carbonate-based electrolytes lead to unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes, which is critical to achieving good cycling performance.
